entities.name: The Threepenny Opera
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: The Threepenny Opera, a groundbreaking musical play created by Elisabeth Hauptmann in collaboration with Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, revolutionized 20th-century theater with its dark, satirical, and socially conscious storytelling. Written in 1928 and first performed in 1929, the opera was a response to the social and economic upheaval of the Weimar Republic, drawing upon themes of love, betrayal, and class struggle. Its innovative blend of music, poetry, and drama has influenced generations of artists, from punk rockers to film directors, making it a cultural touchstone of the modern era. The opera's impact extends beyond the stage, with its subversive critique of capitalism and its exploration of the human condition resonating with audiences worldwide. As a product of the tumultuous 1920s, The Threepenny Opera embodies the spirit of artistic innovation and social commentary that defined this pivotal moment in history.
